title: Gated Activation Steering for Reducing Sycophancy & Hallucination in Medical Question Answering
abstract: arXiv:2608.23666v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Sycophancy and hallucination are persistent failure modes of Large Language Models (LLMs) across domains. However, it becomes particularly consequential in clinical question answering, where responses must remain grounded in the provided context and robust to user pressure. Hallucination can introduce information that is unsupported by the context, while sycophancy can cause a model to abandon a previously correct answer when challenged by the user. translated_title: 门控激活引导用于减少医学问答中的谄媚与幻觉
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.23666v1 公告类型：新 摘要：谄媚和幻觉是大语言模型（LLMs）在各领域中持续存在的失败模式。然而，在临床问答中，这一问题尤为关键，因为回答必须基于所提供的上下文，并对用户的压力保持稳健。幻觉可能引入上下文不支持的信息，而谄媚可能导致模型在用户质疑时放弃先前正确的答案。现有方法，如基于提示的保护机制和始终开启的激活引导，往往分别处理这些行为，或跨轮次进行广泛干预，这可能会不必要地恶化原本正确的回答。为在单一框架内解决这些局限性，我们采用推理时间干预（ITI），通过从对比性临床配对中学习针对幻觉和谄媚的独立引导方向，并应用门控机制，从而联合控制这两种行为。
tldr: 本文提出一种基于门控激活引导的推理时间干预方法，通过独立学习幻觉与谄媚的引导方向并选择性应用，在临床问答中同时减少两类错误而不损害正确回答。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a gated activation steering approach with inference-time intervention, which jointly reduces hallucination and sycophancy in clinical QA by learning separate steering directions and selectively applying them without degrading correct responses.
